Project management experience and skills.

The Assistant Director supervises L&S Advising staff and manages the day-to-day operations of at least one functional area of the office. This position serves as the primary point of contact to subordinates and provides guidance on issues related to academic progress, degree requirements, College policies, and processes. The Assistant Director leads initiatives and coordinates advising services.
Directly supervises the advisor team that provides the full range of academic advising to students and services to department chairs/deans, and faculty.
Develops job descriptions, selects subordinates, and assigns work.
Formulates performance standards in alignment with the University's coaching culture, conducts individual performance evaluations, and recommends corrective action when necessary.
Provides team members guidance and direction on interpreting complex academic policies; sets strategy and develops implementation plans
Functional Area Leadership & Management

Manages functional areas, improves processes and practices, and establishes workflow when none exists or when it requires modification. Oversees and manages the day-to-day operations of the functional area.
Advises team members on complex College policies and procedures.
Plans staff training and inspires positive teamwork.
Serves on committees representing the functional area; participates in short-term and long-term planning.
Provides guidance on issues related to academic progress, degree requirements, College policies, and processes. Leads initiatives and helps coordinate advising services.
Develops tools and implements processes to help students make progress toward degree completion and/or to meet other academic goals.
Leads process analysis and supports improvement efforts.
Professional Development & Growth
Expands upon people management and coaching skills and stays abreast of best practices and innovations in academic advising.
Demonstrated knowledge of advising and counseling techniques.
Demonstrated ability to lead change and innovation.
Demonstrated skill in problem identification and reasoning.
Demonstrates ability to develop original ideas to solve problems.
Demonstrates ability in persuasion and leadership.
Knowledge of University and departmental principles and procedures, or comparable institutional knowledge, involved in risk assessment and evaluating risks as to likelihood and consequences,
